primary_sources: House Committee on Un-American Activities, hearings on the movie industry, 1947

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from the HUAC hearings on the movie industry, 1947

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the House Committee on Un-American Activities hearings on the movie industry, 1947. Paraphrased, not quoted, because the source is after 1929.
stimulus.text: In 1947, the House Committee on Un-American Activities held hearings on communism in the movie industry. The committee called writers and directors to testify about their politics and to name others with communist ties. Ten witnesses, later called the Hollywood Ten, refused to answer the committee's questions, citing their First Amendment rights. They were jailed for contempt of Congress, and studio heads agreed not to hire anyone suspected of communist ties.

stem: The hearings best show that the Red Scare reached beyond the government because

options.text: The committee investigated only soldiers and sailors.
options.misconception: The hearings targeted writers, directors, and actors in Hollywood. Soldiers and sailors were not the committee's subject here.

options.text: Private studios carried out the punishment by denying work.
The Supreme Court ran the hearings in place of Congress.
options.misconception: HUAC was a House committee, not the Supreme Court.

options.text: The hearings ended after a single day of testimony.
options.misconception: Background from the books: the hearings and their effects lasted years, not a single day.

rationales.A: The hearings targeted writers, directors, and actors in Hollywood. Soldiers and sailors were not the committee's subject here.
rationales.B: The studios, private businesses, enforced the blacklist by refusing work to the accused. The punishment reached into private employment, not only government jobs.
rationales.C: HUAC was a House committee, not the Supreme Court. Background from the books: the Court later limited Smith Act convictions, but it never ran HUAC's hearings.
rationales.D: The hearings and their effects lasted years. Background from the books: the Hollywood blacklist lasted until 1960, long after the 1947 hearings.
rationales.general:
1. The government investigated, through HUAC, but the punishment was carried out by private studios.
2. Studio heads agreed not to hire the accused, so the accused lost their livelihoods without any trial.
3. When private employers enforce the punishment, the scare has spread beyond government offices into ordinary workplaces.
Remember: A scare spreads when private institutions enforce what the government only accuses.
